No single model dominates — reported honestly. RMSE is N/A for the ensemble (its score is a rank, not a risk value).
DOES IT WORK?
14/ 15
of the top-15 predicted-riskiest held-out events are truly high-risk (random ≈ 0.4/15 — high-risk events are only 2.7% of the set). Reproduce: python src/orbitguard/ml/predict_demo.py
TASK
Predict each conjunction's final collision probability from CDMs issued ≥2 days before TCA, on the ESA Kelvins dataset (11,942 events, 323 high-risk). The model scores Kelvins CDMs, not yet our live globe (that's Phase 4).
WHAT IT IS

OrbitGuard screens the low-Earth-orbit catalogue for close approaches: it pulls a live CelesTrak snapshot (16,103 objects this run), propagates every object forward, finds the pairs headed for a dangerously close pass, sharpens each to a precise time and miss distance, and ranks them by risk.

Satellite operators

First-pass screen of a fleet against the whole catalogue.

Agencies (NASA / ESA)

Mirrors the front of conjunction-assessment pipelines like SOCRATES / CARA.

Analysts & insurers

Quantify on-orbit collision exposure.

A self-directed engineering project and screening tool — not an operational or safety-certified system. Validate against CelesTrak SOCRATES before any operational use.

ROADMAP
PHASE 0–2.5

v1 — Conjunction screener

Live catalogue → propagate → screen → refine → risk-rank → report + globe.

PHASE 3

ML risk model

Gradient-boosted + CNN models on ESA Kelvins CDMs. See Risk Model.

PHASE 4

Autonomy

Score live conjunctions with the learned model; propose a small avoidance Δv.

PHASE 5

Showcase

Polished writeup + demo — the flagship artifact.
